name: PJ Harvey
who_line: She uses clothes the way she uses a character: to meet the world when the person underneath cannot, or should not, be the story.
who: Polly Jean Harvey is a Dorset songwriter, guitarist, and the only artist to win the Mercury Prize twice. She was bound for sculpture school and Central Saint Martins; the body stayed the object. Visual collaborator across most eras: Maria Mochnacz. Costume collaborators appear later — Annie Mochnacz, Ann Demeulemeester, Todd Lynn.

The 1995 look was a mask she built because she had no self left to show. The 2011 look was armour so she could walk onstage and report a war. Both are costume as protection, not costume as brand. She has called the Patti Smith comparison lazy journalism — treat that as a dismissal of a critic habit, not a denial that she later wore Ann Demeulemeester.
work: Dry (1992) and Rid of Me (1993) are the raw first records: black knit, combat boots, the dress as a charged garment — the first single is literally “Dress.” To Bring You My Love (1995) is the mask she named Joan Crawford on acid. Is This Desire? (1998) retreats. Stories from the City, Stories from the Sea (2000) wins the first Mercury. Uh Huh Her (2004), White Chalk (2007), Let England Shake (2011) — the second Mercury, the war record — The Hope Six Demolition Project (2016), I Inside the Old Year Dying (2023).

For Let England Shake she was reading Harold Pinter’s political essays, seeing Jez Butterworth’s Jerusalem, looking at Goya’s Disasters of War. She told the BBC’s Andrew Marr she did not feel qualified to sing from a political standpoint and would not preach. She kept finding official war artists and poets, “but I couldn’t find the officially appointed war songwriter anywhere.”

quotes.text: I enjoy looking like a tart and thinking like a politician.

I’ve always been attracted by that combination of strength, beauty and vulnerability – and crossing that drag queen line! Obviously, when I play bigger stages I want to give a very strong image, and that comes from wearing a lot of make-up. I would never want to do something that was glamorous and beautiful, full stop, because that would be wrong for what I am doing musically.
That was kind of a mask. It was much more of a mask than I’ve ever had. I was very lost as a person, at that point. I had no sense of self left at all.
quotes.said_to: Dazed & Confused, later reflection on To Bring You My Love (print; circulating via Wikipedia and Vein)

quotes.text: The belt that I wore, it was like a shield of armor. A lot of Ann’s clothes are very protective. There is a lot of closing over in the chest part, and that’s what gives you strength to meet the world or to present to the world whatever it is you are putting out there.
quotes.said_to: Eugene Rabkin, StyleZeitgeist (Let England Shake interview)

why_the_look: She uses clothes the way she uses a character: to meet the world when the person underneath cannot, or should not, be the story.
beliefs: Not church-raised. To Bust she said her mother taught that nature came from God; they weren’t baptized. She does read the Bible in phases. To David Fricke, Rolling Stone, 28 December 1995: “Why take a trip on acid when you can read the Bible?” Childhood records: John Lee Hooker, Howlin’ Wolf, Robert Johnson, Hendrix, Beefheart. A secondary-school rebellion into Duran Duran, Spandau Ballet, Soft Cell.

moments.title: Dry
moments.garments: Black knit, black leggings, Dr. Martens — the pre-1995 baseline. On stage, dresses: halter, sweetheart mini, leopard. 1992 NME cover (Maria Mochnacz): topless, back to camera, unshaven armpit.
moments.designer_season: none / unsourced. No designer on the NME cover.
moments.where_it_lives: NME / Getty. Not freely downloadable. Closest local file is the 1993 Academy still (Rid of Me year).
moments.why_iconic: Body as manifesto before fashion-as-costume. Industry panic; she kept the cover.

moments.title: Rid of Me — Academy, New York
moments.garments: Dark charcoal/black halter-neck dress, deep V, fine all-over shimmer (lurex/glitter knit). Gretsch orange hollow-body. Album cover: nude, wet hair, Maria Mochnacz’s bathroom — Island objected; she kept it.
moments.why_iconic: Last year of the tried-and-true goth kit, and the dress as weapon.

media.caption: PJ Harvey, Academy NYC, 1993. Halter V-neck shimmer dress, Gretsch.

moments.title: To Bring You My Love — Glastonbury catsuit
moments.garments: Hot-pink full-length neoprene catsuit, funnel neck, long sleeves, centre-front zip, worn unzipped to the bust over a black bra. Blue eyeshadow to the brow, fake lashes, red lipstick.
moments.designer_season: none listed. Do not invent one. V&A object record lists no designer.
moments.where_it_lives: V&A accession S.158-2021. Polly Harvey Archive, given by the artist. Material: machine-sewn neoprene. Also worn on the 1995 festival circuit (i-D: Torhout/Werchter).
moments.why_iconic: Joan Crawford on acid, her name for it. A mask, she later said, because she was very lost as a person. Worn-on-body stills are Getty; the object is in the V&A. No legitimate official Glastonbury 1995 upload was verified for embed — BBC archive exists, fan YouTube does not go in this file.

media.caption: V&A S.158-2021. Hot-pink neoprene Glastonbury 24 Jun 1995 catsuit, laid flat. No designer.
Same object + boxed false lashes. V&A conservation layout.
Worn-on-body: Getty / Ian Dickson / Dazed. Object is local.

moments.title: Down by the Water
moments.garments: Flowing dark wig, falsies, red lipstick, slinky red strappy nightgown. High heels in water.
moments.designer_season: none / unsourced. Not a runway piece. Maria Mochnacz to Uncut: Harvey asked for “something red and strappy”; Mochnacz bought a nightgown at TK Maxx in Bristol.
moments.where_it_lives: Official video, dir. Maria Mochnacz. Restored on YouTube; also on pjharvey.net.
moments.why_iconic: That image became the nightly stage dress. The garment can be cheap if the makeup and wig do the work.

media.caption: PJ Harvey — Down by the Water, official video (dir. Maria Mochnacz). Verified on pjharvey.net.

moments.title: Is This Desire? — Cologne
moments.garments: Sleeveless dark top, thin spaghetti strap, messy dark hair, handheld mic. Bettie Page bangs, light-handed makeup.
moments.why_iconic: Retreat from the mask. A woman becoming reacquainted with herself (Hooligan).

moments.title: Stories from the City — lingerie as outerwear / Todd Lynn
moments.garments: Reading 2001: black balconette + leather mini (i-D). Roskilde 2001: thin-strap bra/bikini top + high-waisted skirt. This Is Love / Tate: white leather suit, fringe sleeves — first Todd Lynn outfit, 2001, “tailored leather Elvis jacket with fringes” (Harvey to Vulture, 2023).
moments.designer_season: Lingerie looks: none / unsourced. Leather suit: Todd Lynn, 2001 — not a numbered seasonal RTW citation.
moments.where_it_lives: Roskilde local (low-res). This Is Love stills: i-D / Getty.
moments.why_iconic: City-slicker monochrome, and the first named designer collaboration that is not a house season.

media.caption: Roskilde 2001 Day 3. Bra/bikini top + high-waist skirt. Low-res silhouette.

media.search: PJ Harvey This Is Love white leather suit Tate Modern 2003

moments.title: Uh Huh Her — Spice Girls merch
moments.garments: Glastonbury: top + skirt printed with Spice Girls faces. T in the Park / Eurockéennes: her own merch slashed into tube-dress looks. Jersey minis, tube tops, leather pumps, upcycled band T-shirts. Annie Mochnacz begins making jewellery and clothing for the tour.
moments.where_it_lives: Getty / i-D / Dazed. No local 2004 file. Do not use the 2007 lyrics dress as Uh Huh Her.
moments.why_iconic: Early-00s alt, legs as the protagonist, colour allowed again.

moments.title: White Chalk — lyrics dress
moments.garments: Cream/off-white governess dress, leg-of-mutton sleeves, handwritten/embroidered lyric script from “Grow Grow Grow” and “The Devil,” distressed finish. Built from second-hand materials, adapted from late-18th-century patterns.
moments.where_it_lives: V&A (mannequin) and Royal Festival Hall 2007 (worn onstage). Local files.
moments.why_iconic: English Victorian Gothic. Do not invent a designer beyond Annie Mochnacz. Do not use this dress as Let England Shake.

media.caption: V&A mannequin. Annie Mochnacz White Chalk lyrics dress.
RFH London 2007. Same lyric / leg-of-mutton system worn onstage.

moments.title: Let England Shake — shield of armor
moments.garments: Ann Demeulemeester tour wardrobe: long black or white dress + wide leather corset-belt. Feathered headdress (white/grey or black) — Victorian mourning plume, not carnival. Autoharp. Mercury Prize 2011: feathered headdress, corseted gown, black leather boots, all AD (i-D).
moments.designer_season: Ann Demeulemeester tour wardrobe (house credit; do not invent a numbered season for the custom pieces).
moments.where_it_lives: Coachella, Roskilde, Royal Albert Hall — local files. Mercury stills: Getty / i-D.
moments.why_iconic: She needed armor. The belt was a shield. First meeting with AD: 1995, backstage in Belgium; AD gave her a black leather coat.

media.caption: Coachella 2011. White high-collar, feather spray, autoharp.
Roskilde 2011. White high-neck, feather crown, autoharp.
Royal Albert Hall, 31 Oct 2011. Wide laced leather shield belt, black feather headpiece.

moments.title: The Hope Six Demolition Project
moments.garments: Citizen-journalist uniform: all-black / navy, slim blazers, long unkempt hair. Feathers persist as remnant. Primavera: dark clothes, small pale hair ornaments. Down The Rabbit Hole: ensemble in dark monochrome, three vertical white spots.
moments.designer_season: Designer not sourced for Primavera — do not invent.
moments.why_iconic: Patti adjacency is the point. Uniform, not a hero garment. Do not use Primavera as White Chalk.

media.caption: Down The Rabbit Hole 2016. System shot — uniform, not a hero garment.

moments.title: I Inside the Old Year Dying
moments.garments: Sleeveless floor-length off-white/cream paneled dress (Amsterdam). Tiny Desk: draped dress “the wintry color of a gray alder tree.” Drawing dress: spare Todd Lynn base; one drawing by Polly or a band member before each city. 55 drawings / 55 cities / 71 shows.
moments.designer_season: Todd Lynn tour dress (house credit; not a numbered RTW season).
moments.where_it_lives: Amsterdam local. Tiny Desk: NPR / official YouTube. Drawing dress: pjharvey.net.
moments.why_iconic: Forest / Dorset / Orlam. Cheap material left visible — skeletal process. Safety pin as process, not punk costume.

media.caption: Amsterdam 2023. Todd Lynn tour dress, Firebird, single spotlight.
PJ Harvey: Tiny Desk Concert — official NPR Music upload. Grey-alder Todd Lynn dress.
